newsitem.title: RUSSIA: South Korea consul beaten to death in Russian city.
newsitem.headline: South Korea consul beaten to death in Russian city.

text.p: A South Korean diplomat in Russia's Far East city of Vladivostok was found bludgeoned to death outside his apartment on Tuesday, local police said.
A police spokesman said the killing in the Pacific port city was being investigated, but nobody had been arrested.
In Seoul, Foreign Ministry spokesman Suh Dae-won said consul Choi Duck-keun had been killed on the stairs of his apartment building by unidentified men.

"What we know officially from our investigations is that he was hit on the head by a very heavy tool," he said. His wallet, passport, cash and other personal belongings were untouched, but there was a cut around his midriff.
Suh declined all comment on South Korean media reports suggesting that North Korea was behind the killing.
Korean state radio had said Choi may have been stabbed by a poison needle, but Suh said the cut was much larger than a needle wound.
The radio quoted a Russian witness as saying two Asian men were lurking in the stairwell before Choi entered the building.

It said South Korean diplomats had been warned to take extra precautions following a threat by North Korea to retaliate unless South Korea returned a submarine that intruded into the South two weeks ago.

Pyongyang has demanded the immediate return of the vessel along with its surviving and dead crew. The submarine landed an estimated 26 North Koreans, and of these 22 have been killed and one captured alive during a manhunt.
The domestic Yonhap news agency said Choi was in charge of North Korean affairs at the consulate.
"Speculation had it that Choi might have been murdered by North Koreans especially in consideration of the fact that he was in charge of North Korean affairs," Yonhap said.
Choi was transferred to Vladivostok in 1995 from the consulate in Kiev, where his son now attends university. His wife was with him in Vladivostok. A daughter lives in Seoul.
There is a small community of South Korean businessmen living in Vladivostok, which has A reputation for high crime levels and extremely active organised mafia-like criminal gangs.
